title: Area & Volume
description: Area of triangles, trapezoids, and circles; volume and surface area of prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres, with the right units.

practice.prompt: A triangle has a base of 12 cm and a height of 7 cm. Find its area in cm².

figure.alt: A triangle with base 12 cm and height 7 cm. The height meets the base at a right angle.

hints: A triangle is half of a rectangle: A = ½ · b · h.

practice.prompt: A trapezoid has bases of 8 m and 14 m and a height of 5 m. Find its area in m².
hints: Trapezoid area: A = ½ (b₁ + b₂) · h.

practice.prompt: A rectangular prism (box) is 4 in by 5 in by 6 in. Find its volume in in³.
hints: Volume of a prism = (area of the base) × height.
For a box that is length × width × height.

practice.prompt: A cylinder has radius 3 and height 10. Find its volume. Give the answer in terms of π or round to the hundredths place.
hints: Cylinder: V = (area of the circle base) × height = πr²h.

practice.prompt: A cone has radius 6 and height 8. Find its volume. Give the answer in terms of π or round to the hundredths place.
hints: A cone is ⅓ of a cylinder with the same base and height: V = ⅓ πr²h.

practice.prompt: A square pyramid has a base side of 9 and a height of 10. Find its volume.
hints: Pyramid: V = ⅓ · B · h, where B is the area of the base.
The base is a square, so B = 9² = 81.

practice.prompt: A sphere has radius 3. Find its volume. Give the answer in terms of π or round to the hundredths place.
Find the total surface area of a cube with edge length 5.
hints: Surface area means the total area of all the faces.
A cube has 6 square faces, each 5 × 5.
practice.solution: Each face: 5² = 25. Six faces: 6 · 25 = 150 square units

practice.prompt: A cone and a cylinder have the same radius and the same height. The cone's volume is what fraction of the cylinder's?
hints: Compare the formulas: cylinder V = πr²h, cone V = ⅓ πr²h.
What number is in front of the cone formula?
It takes three full cones of water to fill the matching cylinder.
practice.solution: Cone: ⅓ πr²h. Cylinder: πr²h. The cone is 1/3 of the cylinder.

practice.prompt: A closed cylinder has radius 2 and height 5. Find its total surface area. Give the answer in terms of π or round to the hundredths place.
hints: Think of the parts: two circles (top and bottom) plus the side, which unrolls into a rectangle.

flashcards.back: A = ½ · b · h (height is perpendicular to the base)

figure.alt: Triangle with base b and height h perpendicular to the base.

flashcards.front: Volume of a prism or cylinder
flashcards.back: V = B · h (B = area of the base). Cylinder: V = πr²h

flashcards.front: Volume of a pyramid or cone
flashcards.back: V = ⅓ · B · h. Cone: V = ⅓ πr²h
Length: cm. Area: cm² (square units). Volume: cm³ (cubic units).
If two solids have the same height and the same cross-section area at every level, they have the same volume.
Surface area is multiplied by k²; volume is multiplied by k³.

quiz.prompt: A parallelogram has a base of 11 and a height of 6. Find its area.
A cylinder has a diameter of 8 and a height of 5. Find its volume. Give the answer in terms of π or round to the hundredths place.
A cone has radius 3 and height 7. Find its volume. Give the answer in terms of π or round to the hundredths place.
A pyramid has a rectangular base 6 by 4 and a height of 9. Find its volume.
Find the surface area of a sphere with radius 6. Give the answer in terms of π or round to the hundredths place.
If you double every dimension of a box (length, width, and height), its volume is multiplied by:
hints: Volume = l · w · h, and each one doubles.
quiz.solution: (2l)(2w)(2h) = 8 · lwh. Volume is multiplied by 8 (k³ with k = 2).
